This report: all 6,938 annotated pictures, every object class, every whole-image tag and Clear. Onboarding report: whole-image tags only, 4,141 pictures.
1. This report, and the table quoted in the review

No picture is unlabelled. The earlier table showed 248 pictures at 0 labels because the four size-flagged object classes (Foreign Matter, Fiber, Extraneous Polymer, HEMA) had no column of their own: a picture whose only mark was such an object had nowhere to appear. All four now have their own column, so the 0 row is empty.
A size flag is part of its class, not a second label. Counting the flag beside the class would give every large object two labels; it is counted here once, inside its class.
The onboarding report counts whole-image tags only (4,141 pictures, 15 tags). Object marks and Clear frames sit outside it, which is why its row for one label reads 3,256 and its table stops at 5.

name: Labels considered

rows.value: Every label considered, and every name it appears under

23 names occur in the annotation: 12 whole-image tags, 7 object classes, the HEMA Obstruction tag, two older box classes kept for reference, and Clear. The guide defines 23 classes: 15 tags and 8 object classes. Four of those have no examples yet, the three lens-damage tags and Surface Groove, so they carry no pictures here. The pictures column counts pictures carrying the label, so the rows overlap and do not sum to a picture total.

rows: 32 pictures whose objects the newer annotation calls Extraneous Polymer carry the Fiber flag in the training label list, because the guide defaults an unclear object to Fiber. This workbook counts the flag as annotated.

rows.value: The training label list is unchanged. It is the basis of the train and test split, not a count of the annotation, and every count in this workbook comes from the annotation.
5,531 pictures carry exactly one label. Counted from the annotation, size flags folded into their class, Clear included.
Clear is the largest group: 2,156 pictures show no defect at all. Clear, Missing Primary Package, Cavity Off Center, Package Misalignment and View Obstructed are alone by rule; they carry no co-tag.
The two labels on two-label pictures
649 pictures carry exactly two labels, in 28 distinct pairs.
A pair is counted once, order ignored. A size flag is not a pair member; a picture with a large Bubble is still Bubble plus whatever else it carries.

name: Debris group

rows.value: The Debris group: the four classes that hold debris
Debris is not a class in the guide. It is the group of four object classes below. A picture can hold more than one of them, so the class rows do not add to the group total.

rows.value: Read down the two count columns with the note on the right: several figures in the quoted table count a different unit (boxes carrying one code, boxes in one file group, or a count taken before the 32 objects moved), which is what makes the columns look inconsistent.

One internal check closes the question: a size flag sits inside its class, so a class can never show more flagged objects than pictures. The Extraneous Polymer row shows 168 flagged on 144 pictures, so that row was assembled from two tables.
The two reports we can test agree line by line in the table above: 14,182 objects on 1,130 pictures, both.

name: Definitions

rows.value: One meaning per term, used the same way on every sheet.

rows: One image, counting duplicate copies of the same image once.
One class present on a picture: an object class, a whole-image tag, or Clear.
A box drawn around a defect on a picture. One picture can hold many objects.
The class of a marked object: Bubble, Bubble Cluster, Wet Package, Foreign Matter, Fiber, Extraneous Polymer, HEMA.
One tag on the picture, not on an object: lens presentation, image condition, or the reference tag HEMA Obstruction.
The micron threshold tag on an object. It marks an object that crossed the size threshold and sits inside its class; it is not a label of its own.
A picture with nothing marked on it. It counts as one label.
The four object classes together: Foreign Matter, Fiber, Extraneous Polymer, HEMA. A group, not a class in the guide.
The newest annotation for a picture. Older annotations of the same picture are ignored.
